note: CORE CHECKS. The inputs are synthetic, written to make the sweep exercisable rather than drawn from a real dispatch or a real conversation, but the checked cases test the agent: each carries a condition and handledWhen for its main job, its top guardrail or a fallback path, written from the agent's own prompt and confirmed passing on main in a no-change sweep. A verdict over the unchecked cases is still a claim about the pipeline. NINE cases, eight scored plus one control, and DEFAULT_JUDGE_CONFIG.gates.minCases is 20, so a corpus verdict over this list resolves CAN'T SAY however the judge voted: the floor was set from measured agent non-determinism and eight runs measure that rather than the branch. Eight is one clean baseline plus seven single-axis variations, which is what one change can author honestly across four chat agents; whether to grow to 20 or lower the floor is still open. WHAT THE HARNESS SEEDS for this scope (runners/seedChatOrg.ts): one organization with customPositionName 'Council Member', one electedOffice, and ONE priority titled 'Affordable housing' with description 'Expand the supply of affordable housing downtown.', source user_stated, no target date, anchored as the conversation's priority. The priority's status column is unset, so parsePriorityStatus fills all seven steps as state 'open' with an empty summary: the agent meets a priority where NOTHING has been settled yet, which is the state it meets on the first turn of every real priority and the reason the baseline case is a where-do-we-stand question. Nothing else is seeded. No contacts, so count_contacts answers 0 and there is no audience to propose; no community issues, so read_community_issues comes back empty; no past outreach; no cards in the thread, so anchorSummaries is empty; and the constituent-data pair is off because the district gate fails, not because a row is missing. The seeder sets organization.positionId, the half of that gate in our own database, and the id it sets is a real one (the internal election-api id for Cheyenne City Council Ward 1), but only the two integration tests ever stub an election-api reply for it (runners/seedChatOrg.tools.integration.test.ts and runners/chat.integration.test.ts, each re-spying ElectionsService.getPositionById); sweep.eval.test.ts, the arm that drives judged turns, installs nothing and inherits the null useTestService pins getPositionById to null unconditionally for every suite it boots, a credentialed deployment included, so resolveByOrgSlug returns null and districtFilters is null on every run this harness makes. The Databricks credential query_constituent_data additionally needs is a second gate behind that one, never reached. A credentialed deployment does not fix it either, because that stub is installed before any credential is read; what the real id buys is that it no longer fails HARDER than an uncredentialed one, a synthetic id having come back as a 404 turned NotFoundException out of loadContext and failed the whole turn. Letting the sweep arm's getPositionById reach election-api is what would register the pair. The integration test, driven against the chief_of_staff handler because it shares this scope's resolver and table allowlist, proves the handler and the resolver wire up correctly when a position is supplied, not that any environment supplies one. Live tools are update_priority_status, present_outreach_proposal, present_contacts, present_past_outreach, read_past_outreach, web_search, read_community_issues, describe_filter_dimensions, count_contacts and crud_saved_filters. Varied along: what the seeded priority row and its seven empty steps already carry against what needs a live search; a turn that must WRITE (update_priority_status, with a one-sentence next action) against turns that only read; one right answer against a judgement call; a turn answerable from the priority context alone against one needing a tool call; a well-formed request against a vague one; a turn the agent must decline with the exact off-topic guardrail line; and a request for an audience the seeded CRM cannot supply, which is the capability-honesty probe. Serve vocabulary throughout per docs/product-vocabulary.md: constituents, office, term, and never voters, election or ballot. 'Outreach campaign' is the permitted sense of campaign in Serve, so the outreach case uses it deliberately. The vague turn is modelled on the rambling-preamble cases in the Chief of Staff golden bench (src/chats/general/chief-of-staff/evals/cases/input_robustness.yaml), which is the nearest suite that has already discriminated on intent-over-surface-form; priority_flow has no eval suite of its own, so the other seven questions are written here rather than reused.

cases.question: What's a good place near city hall to take my staff for lunch on Friday?
cases.condition: An off-topic request with nothing to do with the priority. The assistant must decline with a line steering back to this priority and say nothing else.
cases.handledWhen: the reply declines and points back to working this priority, and recommends no restaurant or lunch spot. Any lunch suggestion is not handled.

cases.question: What do we actually know about how many affordable units downtown have been permitted in the last 3 years?
cases.condition: No permit data is on file for this priority. The assistant must never invent a number: every count it states comes from a source it can name, and anything else is called an estimate with where to check it.
cases.handledWhen: any permit count the reply gives is tied to a named source, and when it has no sourced figure it says so and says where the official could get it, such as the city planning or permitting office. A specific number of permitted units with no named source is not handled.

cases.question: We settled the problem definition at last week's session: the downtown supply gap is the binding constraint, not demand. Get that recorded and tell me what's next.
cases.condition: The official reports a settled problem definition and asks for it to be recorded. The assistant must say what changed for the official in plain terms, never talk about records, status fields, steps or tools, and move them to what comes next.
cases.handledWhen: the reply confirms the problem as the official stated it (the downtown supply gap, not demand) and names the concrete work that comes next. Explaining internal mechanics such as status fields, steps being updated or tools is not handled, and a plain acknowledgment that it is noted is fine. A reply with no concrete next work is not handled.

cases.question: Put together an outreach campaign to the constituents most affected by this so I can hear from them before the vote.
Where do we stand on this priority, and what should I do next?
Housing costs downtown are out of control. Help me say what the actual problem is in one or two sentences I could defend at a council meeting.
Who do I need to hear from before I take a public position on this?
ok so this one keeps coming up and i keep punting on it, honestly what do i even do here
What are my realistic options on this one, including doing nothing?
